references.text: The fulfillment of the prophecy about the great cry in Egypt when all the firstborn died and a wailing was heard in every house.
God heard Israel's cry under slavery in Egypt; now the Egyptians themselves will experience a great cry.
Amos describes an unprecedented judgment from the Lord, parallel to the unique disaster that struck Egypt.
Joel describes a day without equal, one that has never happened before and will never happen again, using the same language as Exodus 11:6.
Daniel uses similar language about a unique time of distress unlike any other.
The hail plague is also described as without parallel in Egypt's history, following the same pattern as 11:6.
Jesus uses the same expression regarding the great tribulation that will be without equal in world history.
John describes an earthquake unmatched since mankind came to earth, using parallel language about an unprecedented judgment.
Uses an identical formula to show that the tenth plague was the culmination of a series of unique judgments.
